e0840d1d2e91c18648cf520bbb868484f3079f63: Alpe d'Huez offers 140 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 38 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Alpe d'Huez's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. On snow reliability, Alpe d'Huez is in a strong position thanks to its summit at 3330 m — even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well into April. The village at 1860 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. A stay in Alpe d'Huez is clearly expensive: 68€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and high-altitude restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Alpe d'Huez lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most skiers without disappointing.
e09150ae477276414c4a62ab2841846e325c0cad: La Toussuire is one of the rare resorts offering more than 310 km of runs, a huge ski area that even the fastest skiers would not cover in a week. With 61 lifts and 35 listed runs, it is a destination that can absorb large numbers of visitors without ever feeling crowded. La Toussuire's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2620 m and a village at 1750 m, snow reliability at La Toussuire is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause difficulties early in the season, but conditions recover quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. A stay at La Toussuire is clearly on the expensive side: 59€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the dearest in the Alps. It is the price of quality, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, La Toussuire delivers on its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
